Department of Aeronautical Engineering



Department Overview:

About the Department:	

The Department of Aeronautical Engineering at M.A.M. School of Engineering was started in the year 2010. It is dedicated to shaping future engineers in the dynamic and highly specialized field of aerospace. The program is designed to equip students with the knowledge and skills needed to design, develop, test, and maintain aircraft, spacecraft, and related systems. With a combination of theoretical knowledge and practical applications, the department focuses on cutting-edge technologies in aerodynamics, propulsion, avionics, and materials science.



The department boasts experienced faculty, modern laboratories, and a curriculum that integrates core engineering concepts with aerospace-specific technologies. Students are trained to meet the growing demands of the aerospace industry, preparing them to become successful professionals and innovators in both national and international aerospace sectors.



About Course:

Aeronautical Engineering is one of the most challenging fields of engineering with a wide scope of growth. This field deals with the development of new technology in the field of aviation, space exploration and defence systems. It specializes in designing, construction, development, testing, operation and maintenance of both commercial and military aircraft and their components as well as missiles. Aeronautical industry is at the forefront of scientific and technological developments that make it one of the most technically advanced and exciting industries to work with.



It deals with all the technical details and mechanisms behind all flying bodies. It specializes in the designing, construction, development, testing, operation and maintenance of both commercial and military aircrafts, spacecrafts and their components as well as satellites and missiles. Aeronautical Industry provides an environment for innovation and excellent career development.

Value Added Course – Fundamentals of Drone Technologies:

The Department of Aeronautical Engineering conducted a value-added course on Fundamentals of Drones Technologies, designed to provide participants with foundational knowledge and practical skills in drone technology. The course covered key topics such as UAV design, aerodynamics, navigation systems, and real-world applications across industries. Hands-on sessions included drone assembly, programming, and flight simulations, enabling participants to gain in-depth technical expertise. Delivered by experienced faculty and industry experts, the course emphasized innovation, safety protocols, and career opportunities in the rapidly growing field of unmanned aerial systems. Participants received certifications, enhancing their academic and professional profiles.



Value Added Course – Nano Satellites:

	The Department of Aeronautical Engineering organized a value-added course on Nano Satellites, aimed at equipping participants with essential knowledge and skills in small satellite technology. The course covered key aspects such as satellite design, subsystem integration, communication systems, and mission planning. Practical sessions focused on prototyping nano satellite components and using simulation tools for mission analysis. Led by seasoned faculty and industry experts, the program highlighted the expanding significance of nano satellites in communication, research, and space exploration. Participants received certifications, boosting their expertise and opening avenues for innovation and careers in the aerospace sector.



Value Added Course – Learnathon 2023:

Learnathon 2023 was an innovative and immersive learning event designed to inspire curiosity, foster creativity, and promote skill development across diverse domains. With a focus on hands-on learning and interdisciplinary collaboration, the event offered a wide range of workshops, seminars, and challenges tailored for students, professionals, and enthusiasts. Topics included cutting-edge technologies, entrepreneurship, and personal growth strategies, delivered by experts and industry leaders. Learnathon 2023 encouraged our aeronautical students to explore new ideas, develop practical solutions, and connect with like-minded individuals. The event’s inclusive and dynamic approach provided a unique platform for knowledge exchange and personal advancement.

Department of Aeronautical Engineering



Facilities:



CESSNA Aircraft:































The Aeronautical Engineering Department offers access to a Cessna aircraft as a valuable educational resource. This aircraft serves as a practical platform for hands-on learning, allowing students to explore aircraft systems, aerodynamics, propulsion, and maintenance in a real-world context. Equipped with detailed technical documentation, the Cessna enhances experiential learning through inspections, assembly tasks, and system troubleshooting exercises. It supports research projects, providing insights into general aviation and flight mechanics. By integrating theoretical concepts with practical applications, the Cessna aircraft fosters a deeper understanding of aerospace engineering principles, preparing students for careers in aviation and aerospace industries

















2. Propulsion Laboratory:

 























The Propulsion Laboratory in the Aeronautical Engineering Department is a cutting-edge facility dedicated to the study of aircraft and spacecraft propulsion systems. It offers advanced equipment, including engine test benches, fuel systems, and performance monitoring tools, enabling students to analyze the mechanics of jet engines, turboprops, and piston engines. The lab facilitates hands-on learning through experiments in combustion, thrust measurement, and engine efficiency, bridging theoretical knowledge with practical applications. Supporting research and development, the lab also promotes innovation in sustainable propulsion technologies. This comprehensive facility prepares students for industry and research roles, emphasizing modern propulsion systems and aerospace advancements.

















3. Aircraft Structures Laboratory:

























The Aircraft Structures Laboratory in the Aeronautical Engineering Department provides a state-of-the-art environment for studying the design, analysis, and testing of aircraft structures. Equipped with advanced tools like universal testing machines, strain gauges, and non-destructive testing equipment, the lab supports experiments in material strength, stress analysis, and structural behaviour under load. Students gain hands-on experience with composite materials, riveted joints, and fuselage sections, bridging theoretical concepts with practical applications. The lab also facilitates research on lightweight and high-performance materials, promoting innovation in aerospace design. This comprehensive facility prepares students for careers in aircraft design, manufacturing, and structural engineering.

















4. Aerodynamics Laboratory:

























The Aerodynamics Laboratory in the Aeronautical Engineering Department features a modern wind tunnel for analysing airflow and aerodynamic forces. This facility enables students to study lift, drag, and flow visualization around various shapes and aircraft models. Equipped with sensors and data acquisition systems, it supports experiments on boundary layers, turbulence, and pressure distribution. The lab bridges theoretical aerodynamics with practical insights, fostering a deeper understanding of flight dynamics and design optimization. It also supports research into innovative designs, including UAVs and sustainable aviation. The Aerodynamics Lab prepares students for careers in aerospace engineering by emphasizing hands-on learning and experimentation.

About the Department:	

     The Department of Biomedical Engineering at M.A.M. School of Engineering was established in 2022, reflecting the institution's commitment to emerging and healthcare technologies. The department aims to bridge engineering principles with medical sciences, preparing students to contribute to the design and development of advanced medical devices, diagnostic equipment, and healthcare innovations. The department provides strong foundations in electronics, physiology, medical instrumentation, and imaging techniques. The faculty team is dynamic and blends academic strength with industry experience, ensuring students receive both theoretical knowledge and hands-on exposure. The Department is actively involved in organizing workshops and guest lectures by industry experts, providing students with valuable exposure to current trends and practices in the biomedical field. It encourages student participation in technical competitions and sports, fostering both intellectual growth and team spirit. The department has established collaborations with hospitals and biomedical firms to facilitate internships and industrial visits, helping students gain practical experience and industry insights. Additionally, it supports students in undertaking projects related to healthcare technology and patient care, nurturing innovation and problem-solving skills. Since its inception, the department has made its mark through notable student achievements in both academics and extracurricular activities, reflecting its strong focus on holistic development.

About the Course:

      Biomedical course at M.A.M. School of Engineering is designed to equip students with the knowledge and skills needed to innovate at the intersection of engineering and healthcare. The curriculum covers a broad spectrum of subjects including human anatomy and physiology, medical electronics, biomedical instrumentation, medical imaging, biomaterials, and rehabilitation engineering. Emphasizing both theory and practical application, the course includes laboratory sessions, industrial training, and project work that prepare students for careers in medical device design, healthcare IT, hospital management, and research. With the growing demand for advanced healthcare solutions, this program offers students a strong foundation to pursue opportunities in the biomedical industry, hospitals, research centers, and higher education.

. Lab Facilities:

Biomedical Instrumentation Lab :

Biomedical Instrumentation Laboratory at M.A.M. School of Engineering provides students with hands-on experience in operating and analyzing various medical instruments used in healthcare. The lab focuses on the measurement of physiological parameters such as ECG, EEG, EMG, blood pressure, and respiration rate, enabling students to understand the working principles behind diagnostic and monitoring equipment. Students are trained to design and test bio-amplifiers, filters, and signal conditioning circuits, as well as to calibrate and troubleshoot biomedical devices. Equipped with ECG machines, EMG recorders, pulse oximeters, blood pressure monitors, defibrillator trainers, and multiparameter simulators, the lab offers practical exposure to industry-standard tools. Simulation software like MATLAB and LabVIEW is also used to analyze biosignals and develop healthcare solutions. Through these activities, the lab aims to develop the technical skills required for careers in hospital equipment management, medical device development, and clinical engineering.



Diagnostic and Therapeutic Equipment  Laboratory:

 Diagnostic and Therapeutic Equipment Laboratory at M.A.M. School of Engineering is designed to train students in the functioning, testing, and maintenance of advanced medical equipment used in diagnosis and therapy. The lab provides practical exposure to devices such as ultrasound scanners, ventilators, defibrillators, diathermy units, and patient monitoring systems. Students learn the principles behind imaging systems, therapeutic modalities, and life-support equipment, along with safety standards and calibration procedures. Hands-on sessions help students understand the operation and troubleshooting of diagnostic tools like ECG and EEG machines, as well as therapeutic devices such as shortwave diathermy and nebulizers. The lab also encourages students to simulate and analyze equipment performance using modern software tools. This practical training equips students with the skills needed for roles in clinical engineering, hospital equipment maintenance, and medical device industries.







Bio Science  Laboratory:



        The bioscience lab at M.A.M. School of Engineering provides a strong foundation for students, particularly those in the biomedical engineering department, to understand the biological and physiological concepts that support biomedical technologies. This laboratory is designed to connect engineering with life sciences, making it an important part of the academic program for students preparing for careers in biomedical fields. The lab is equipped with microscopes, hemocytometers, colorimeters, centrifuges and blood grouping kits,  allowing students to perform a range of experiments. These include the estimation of hemoglobin, blood grouping and Rh typing, the study of the human skeletal system and major organs, observation of cell division processes like mitosis and meiosis, and enzyme activity assays. Through these practical sessions, students gain valuable hands-on experience that deepens their understanding and prepares them for real-world applications in medical device development, diagnostics, and healthcare. The bioscience lab supports theoretical learning in subjects such as human physiology, biochemistry, and pathology, ensuring a comprehensive educational experience.

1. Introduction:

About the Department:	

The Department of Electrical and Electronics  Engineering at M.A.M. School of Engineering was started in the year 2010. It is dedicated to shaping future engineers in the dynamic and highly specialized field of Electrical and Electronics . The program is designed to equip students with the knowledge and skills needed to design, develop, test, and maintain   electrical and electronics  systems. With a combination of theoretical knowledge and practical applications, the department focuses on cutting-edge technologies in control systems, automotive electronics and renewable energy

Electrical & Electronics Engineering (EEE) has become more and more important in today's energy-dependent world to fulfill the changing needs of society. Over the years, innovations in this discipline have transformed everyday life, from powering homes to advancing smart technologies.

The department boasts experienced faculty, modern laboratories, and a curriculum that integrates core engineering concepts. Electrical engineers have diverse career opportunities across various sectors, including power generation, renewable energy, manufacturing, telecommunications, and aerospace. They can find work as design engineers, control systems engineers, power systems engineers, or in research and development roles. Specific industries offering opportunities include automotive, electronics, and the development of smart technologies. Students are trained to meet the growing demands of the electrical and electronics industry, preparing them to become successful professionals and innovators in both national and international  sectors.



About Course:

Electrical and Electronics  Engineering is one of the most challenging fields of engineering with a wide scope of growth. This field deals with the development of new technology in the field of electrical power generation distribution electronics,  and defence systems. It specializes in designing, construction, development, testing, operation and maintenance of both commercial and military aircraft and their components as well as missiles. Aeronautical industry is at the forefront of scientific and technological developments that make it one of the most technically advanced and exciting industries to work with.

INTRODUCTION

ABOUT THE DEPARTMENT

The Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE) at M.A.M. School of Engineering (MAMSE), Siruganur, established in the academic year 2010, offers a four-year B.E. program designed to provide strong foundations in electronic devices, embedded systems, and modern communication technologies. The department is committed to delivering high-quality technical education through a balanced approach of theory and practical learning. It is equipped with well-established and specialized laboratories such as Circuits  and Devices Lab, LIC/Digital Lab, VLSI Lab, Microprocessor and Microcontroller Lab, Networks and Communication sysytems Lab, which enable students to gain hands-on experience and industry-relevant skills. The core focus areas of study include circuit analysis, signals and systems, digital electronics, VLSI, and embedded systems. With a vision to develop competent engineers with strong ethical values, the department strives to nurture innovation and problem-solving abilities to meet global technological demands

OBJECTIVES

Vision

To excel in the evolving domains of Electronics and Communication Engineering by imparting comprehensive knowledge, problem solving skills and innovative ideas to find solutions for complex engineering problems to meet the needs of industry and society.

Mission

To inculcate conducive and innovative teaching learning through ICT tools and    

 E learning platforms.

To acquire ethical and value based education to address the industrial and societal needs. 

To Establish a Centre of Excellence in emerging fields through industry and institute interaction.

To promote employable skills by enhancing communication skills, entrepreneurial skills, leadership skills with universal human values



Program Specific Outcomes

PSO1: Design, develop and analyze electronic systems through application of Integrated circuits and digital principles.

PSO2: Design, develop and analyze communication systems through application of fundamentals from communication principles, signal processing, and RF System Design & Electromagnetics.



Programme Educational Objectives (PEOs)



PEO 1 : Graduates will be able to apply the concepts of Electronics and Communication Engineering in the field of Embedded and VLSI Systems ,IoT, Artificial Intelligence, Communication  and Networking .

PEO 2 : Graduates will be able to  use the cutting edge software and hardware tools for analysing, designing  the innovative products 

PEO 3 : Graduates will be able to inculcate managerial and entrepreneurial skills in the field of engineering and technology.

PROGRAM OUTCOMES (PO’S)



PO1

Engineering	Knowledge: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems. 

PO2

Problem Analysis: Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyze complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.

PO3

Design/Development of Solutions: Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.

PO4

Conduct Investigations of Complex Problems: Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions.

PO5

Modern Tool Usage: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modeling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations.

PO6

The Engineer and Society: Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional engineering practice.

PO7

Environment and Sustainability: Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable development.

PO8

Ethics: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice.

PO9

Individual and Team work: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings.

PO10

Communication: Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large, such as, being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and receive clear instructions.

PO11

Project Management and Finance:  Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and management principles and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.

PO12

Life-long Learning: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.

Program Specific Outcomes (PSOs):

PSO1

Graduates will be able to apply the concepts of Electronics and Communication Engineering in the field of Embedded and VLSI Systems, IoT, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Communication and Networking. 

PSO2

Graduates will be able to use the cutting edge software and hardware tools for analyzing, designing and implementing products.

PSO3

Graduates will be able to adapt to emerging electronics and communication technologies and develop innovative solutions for existing and newer problems.

PROGRAM EDUCATIONAL OBJECTIVES (PEOs) 

Program Educational Objectives (PEOs)



The graduates shall be able 



Effectuating success in careers by exploring with the design, digital and computational analysis of engineering systems, experimentation and testing, smart manufacturing, technical services, and research



Amalgamating effectively with stakeholders to update and improve their core competencies and abilities to ethically compete in the ever-changing multicultural global enterprise. 



To encourage multi-disciplinary research and development to foster advanced technology, and to nurture innovation and entrepreneurship in order to compete successfully in the global economy. 



To globally share and apply technical knowledge to create new opportunities that proactively advances our society through team efforts and to solve various challenging technical, environmental and societal problems. 



To create world class mechanical engineers capable of practice engineering ethically with a solid vision to become great leaders in academia, industries and society. 







PROGRAM OUTCOMES (POs) 



PO 1 GRADUATE ATTRIBUTE Engineering knowledge: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals, and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.



PO 2 Problem analysis: Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyse complex engineering problems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and engineering sciences.



PO 3 Design/development of solutions: Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations. 



PO 4 Conduct investigations of complex problems: Use research-based knowledge and research methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the information to provide valid conclusions. 



PO 5 Modern tool usage: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern engineering and IT tools including prediction and modelling to complex engineering activities with an understanding of the limitations. 



PO 6 The engineer and society: Apply reasoning informed by the contextual knowledge to assess societal, health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional engineering practice.



PO 7 Environment and sustainability: Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable development. 



PO8 Ethics: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of the engineering practice. 



PO9 Individual and team work: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings. 



PO10 Communication: Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering community and with society at large, such as, being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and receive clear instructions. 



PO11 Project management and finance: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering and management principles and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments. 



PO12 Life-long learning: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change. 



PROGRAM SPECIFIC OUTCOMES (PSOs) 



On successful completion of the Mechanical Engineering Degree programme, the Graduates shall exhibit the following: 



1. Apply the knowledge gained in Mechanical Engineering for design and development and manufacture of engineering systems.



 2. Apply the knowledge acquired to investigate research-oriented problems in mechanical engineering with due consideration for environmental and social impacts. 



3. Use the engineering analysis and data management tools for effective management of multidisciplinary projects.

MECHANICAL ENGINEERING OPPORTUNITY



Mechanical engineering offers a wide range of career paths across diverse industries. Engineers can specialize in areas like design, manufacturing, automation, robotics, and sustainable energy, with opportunities in automotive, aerospace, energy, construction, and research & development. Emerging fields like additive manufacturing, AI, and IoT are also creating new avenues for mechanical engineers. 



Specific career paths and industries: 



 Automotive: Design and production of vehicles, including engine systems, chassis, and control systems. 







   Aerospace: Design and development of aircraft, spacecraft, and related systems. 









  Manufacturing: Process optimization, automation, quality control, and product development. 



  Energy: Design and maintenance of power plants, renewable energy systems, and energy efficiency solutions. 



















  Robotics and Automation: Design, development, and implementation of robotic systems for various applications. 







  Research and Development: Innovation and development of new technologies and products. 























  Consulting: Providing expert advice and solutions to clients in various industries. 







  Government and Military: Serving in various roles, including design, development, and testing of military equipment. 













Emerging fields: 

Additive Manufacturing (3D Printing): 

Design and production of complex parts using 3D printing technology. 











Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Manufacturing: 

Integrating AI into manufacturing processes to improve efficiency and quality. 



Industrial Internet of Things (IoT): 

Connecting machines and systems to collect data and improve decision-making. 









Renewable Energy Technology: 

Developing and implementing renewable energy solutions, such as solar and wind power.

STRENGTH OF MATERIALS LABORATORY















DYNAMICS OF MACHINES  LABORATORY

Dynamics Lab is to impart practical knowledge on design and analysis of mechanisms in machine tools and automobiles. The students are doing the experiments related to their theory subjects like Engineering Mechanics, Machines and Mechanisms and Fundamentals of Vibration and Noise. Various equipment like governors, gyroscopes, balancing machines and universal vibration facilities are available to understand machine dynamics. The working models of simple mechanisms like gears, cams and followers are very much useful to understand Basic Mechanical Engineering subjects for 1st year students. The vibration equipment is well established in the dynamics lab. It is used to measure the vibration behavior under induced and self excitation conditions.











FLUID MECHANICS AND MACHINERY LABORATORY























ENGINEERING PRACTICES LABORATORY















CNC MACHINES











MANUFACTURING TECHNOLOGY LABORATORY

Objective of this course is to Study and practice the various operations that can be performed in lathe, shaper, milling machines and to equip them with the practical knowledge required in the core industries. And also to give a broad understanding of conventional and non-conventional machining processes with an emphasis on the characterization techniques. This course also familiarizes students with the scientific principles governing various machining processes.













METROLOGY LABORATORY

The purpose of this laboratory is to familiarize students with measuring instruments, to study various methods of measurement, to learn proper measuring techniques for the measurement of mass, length, angle and quality, and to express the results of calculations so as to correctly imitate the effects of measurement uncertainty. This lab facilitates the students to observe whether the result is given with adequate rightness and accuracy for a particular need or not.







CAD / CAM LABORATORY





































HEAT TRANSFER LABORATORY

To study the heat transfer phenomena predict the relevant coefficient using implementation and also study the performance of refrigeration cycle / components.





























THERMAL ENGINEERING LABORATORY

In this laboratory, students will have the opportunity to study the working principle of IC engines (both SI and CI engines), performance and characteristics in terms of heat balancing, economical speed variations, air fuel ratio influence on the engine to reinforce classroom theory by having the student perform required tests, analyze subsequent data, and present the results in a professionally prepared report.

The machines and equipment used to determine experimental data include cut models of 4stroke diesel engine, 2stroke petrol engine, 4stroke and two stroke petrol engines with required specifications, Multi cylinder SI engine, Single cylinder Diesel engine for performance and speed test which is suitable for tests on variable compression ratios.

About the Department:	

The department of Mechatronics Engineering was started in the year 2012 as one of the core engineering disciplines of the institute. The department has well developed laboratory infrastructure which bridges the gap between industry and academia. The department regularly invites people from the industry to interact with the faculty and students to update them with the current Technologies and Industrial needs.



MAMSE offers under graduate Program of B.E Mechatronics Engineering, providing students with a comprehensive understanding of robotics, automation, control systems, sensors, and other relevant technologies.



The department is well-known for its cutting-edge facilities and multidisciplinary faculty, which make the programme exceptional at our institution. In addition to its regular curriculum, the department also conducts a wide range of other activities, including industrial consulting, industrial training, academic and industry-collaborated research, workshop, seminar, and conference planning.

5. Lab Facilities:



Industrial Automation Lab

	The Industrial Automation Lab is a specialized training and experimentation facility designed to provide students with hands-on experience in the principles, technologies, and systems used in modern automated industries. The lab bridges the gap between theoretical learning and practical application by allowing students to design, program, simulate, and operate automated processes and equipment.

Develop practical skills in working with Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), Human-Machine Interfaces (HMIs), sensors, actuators, and industrial communication networks. Enable students to design, program, test, and troubleshoot automated systems used in manufacturing and process industries.



Robotics & Machine Vision System Lab

	The Robotics & Machine Vision System Lab is a state-of-the-art facility designed to provide students with hands-on experience in the design, programming, integration, and testing of robotic systems combined with intelligent vision technologies. This lab equips students with both theoretical understanding and practical skills needed for developing autonomous and semi-autonomous systems used in modern industries.  Teach fundamental and advanced concepts in robotics, including kinematics, dynamics, control, and motion planning. Provide practical training in integrating vision systems with robotic platforms for perception, inspection, and navigation tasks. Enable students to design, program, and test robotic applications for real-world industrial and research problems.

Design & Modeling Lab 

The Design & Modeling Lab is a specialized facility focused on equipping students with the knowledge and skills necessary to conceptualize, design, and model mechanical and mechatronic systems. This lab combines the principles of mechanical design, computer-aided design (CAD), and virtual modeling to help students turn ideas into real, manufacturable products. By using state-of-the-art software and tools, students gain practical experience in transforming theoretical concepts into tangible, functional designs
